extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in differential geometry / geometric analysis (Ricci flow)
extracted.subtask_description: Reading and applying the Hamilton–Perelman theory of Ricci flow: definitions, monotone functionals (Perelman’s F, W, λ, µ, ν), maximum principles for tensors, and related structure theorems used in analysing Ricci flow solutions (breathers, solitons, curvature nonnegativity, strong/advanced maximum principles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breather definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric g_ij(t) evolving by the Ricci flow is called a breather if for some t1 < t2 and α > 0 the metrics α g_ij(t1) and g_ij(t2) differ only by a diffeomorphism; the case α = 1, α < 1, α > 1 correspond to steady, shrinking and expanding breathers, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ricci solitons are trivial breathers (metrics differ by diffeomorphism and scaling for every pair t1,t2). This definition is used to characterize periodic-orbit-like behaviour in the moduli of metrics modulo diffeomorphism and scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman F-functional (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: F(g, f) = ∫_M (R + |∇f|^2) e^{-f} dV, defined on the space of Riemannian metrics g and smooth functions f on M, where R is the scalar curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a Lyapunov-type functional for the Ricci flow; variations and monotonicity properties (under a coupled flow for g and f) are key tools for analyzing fixed points and solitons.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation formula for F
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (Perelman): If δg_ij = v_ij and δf = h, then the first variation δF(v_ij,h) is given by an integral formula involving v_ij(R_ij + ∇_i∇_j f), the trace v = g^{ij} v_ij, and h and their Laplacians and gradients (explicit formula in Lemma 1.5.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This variation formula is the technical basis for proving monotonicity of F under the appropriate coupled flow; it shows which combination of curvature and Hessian terms controls first-order changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coupled flow for monotonicity of F
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the coupled evolution ∂_t g_ij = -2R_ij, ∂_t f = -Δf + |∇f|^2 - R. Under this flow d/dt F(g(t),f(t)) = 2 ∫ |R_ij + ∇_i∇_j f|^2 e^{-f} dV, i.e., F is nondecreasing in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotonicity is strict unless the flow is a steady gradient soliton. Also ∫ e^{-f} dV is constant under this coupled flow, allowing variational arguments (solve f backward in time to compare infima).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of ∫ e^{-f} dV under the coupled flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the coupled flow for (g,f), the quantity ∫_M e^{-f} dV is constant in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conservation is used as a normalization constraint when defining λ(g) as an infimum over f with ∫ e^{-f} dV = 1; it allows solving the evolution for f backward in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: λ-energy (definition and spectral interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: λ(g) = inf_{f, ∫ e^{-f} dV = 1} F(g,f). Equivalently, if u = e^{-f/2}, λ(g) is the first eigenvalue of the operator -4Δ + R, with minimizer u_0 > 0 and f_0 = -2 log u_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: λ(g) is invariant under diffeomorphism and is achieved by a smooth positive minimizer satisfying an Euler–Lagrange equation (2Δ f_0 - |∇f_0|^2 + R = -λ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of λ along Ricci flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary: λ(g(t)) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow and the monotonicity is strict unless the solution is a steady gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One constructs f(t) by solving the backward heat equation from a minimizer at some time and uses Proposition 1.5.3 to compare λ at different times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale-invariant λ̄ and expanding monotonicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Define λ̄(g) = λ(g) V(g)^{2/n} where V(g) is the volume. Corollary: λ̄ is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow whenever it is nonpositive; monotonicity is strict except for gradient expanding solitons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to analyze expanding breathers: expanding breather must be an expanding gradient soliton; λ̄ is invariant under diffeomorphism and scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact steady/expanding breather ⇒ Einstein (compact case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition: On a compact manifold, a steady or expanding breather is necessarily an Einstein metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences follow from monotonicity of λ and λ̄ and classification of equality cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's W-functional (definition and invariances)
rubrics_metrics.description: W(g,f,τ) = ∫_M [τ(R + |∇f|^2) + f - n] (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV where τ>0; W is invariant under simultaneous scaling of τ and g and under diffeomorphisms: W(a ϕ^* g, ϕ^* f, a τ) = W(g,f,τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: W is the scale-sensitive functional used to study shrinking solitons and is the basis for µ and ν energies.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation formula for W
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma: If δg_ij = v_ij, δf = h, δτ = η then δW(v,h,η) equals a (somewhat lengthy) integral expression involving τ(R_ij + ∇_i∇_j f), trace terms, h, η and the normalization factor (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} (see Lemma 1.5.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to the variation for F; the explicit formula identifies the combination of curvature, Hessian and scaling terms controlling first variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coupled flow for monotonicity of W (and evolution of τ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider ∂_t g_ij = -2R_ij, ∂_t f = -Δf + |∇f|^2 - R + n/(2τ), ∂_t τ = -1, with the normalization ∫ (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV = 1. Then d/dt W = 2τ ∫ |R_ij + ∇_i∇_j f - (1/(2τ)) g_ij|^2 (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotonicity is strict unless one is on a shrinking gradient soliton. Also the weighted volume ∫ (4πτ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV is constant under the flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: µ and ν energies (definitions and existence of minimizers)
rubrics_metrics.description: µ(g,τ) = inf_{f, normalization} W(g,f,τ); ν(g) = inf_{τ>0} µ(g,τ). The µ infimum is achieved by a smooth positive minimizer u satisfying a nonlinear Euler–Lagrange equation; µ corresponds to the best constant of a logarithmic Sobolev inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence follows since the nonquadratic (entropy) term is subcritical; minimizers satisfy an elliptic PDE (see (1.5.13)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of µ and characterization of shrinkers
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary: µ(g(t), τ - t) is nondecreasing along the Ricci flow; monotonicity is strict unless on a shrinking gradient soliton. Consequently, a shrinking breather is necessarily a shrinking gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses backward heat evolution for f and invariance/scaling properties of W and µ; equality cases characterize shrinkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barrier function existence for maximum principle (Lemma 2.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a smooth function f on M with f ≥ 1, f(x) → ∞ as d_0(x,x_0) → ∞, and controlled derivatives: |∇f| and |∇^2 f| bounded (relative bounds) on M × [0,T] for a Ricci flow with uniformly bounded curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed by averaging a compactly supported radial test function over tangent spaces and using Hessian comparison and Shi's estimates; used as a spatial barrier in maximum principle arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle for scalar curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition: If scalar curvature R of the solution g_ij(t) is nonnegative at t=0, then it remains nonnegative for 0 ≤ t ≤ T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the PDE ∂_t R = ΔR + 2|Ric|^2, the barrier f from Lemma 2.1.1, and weak maximum principle applied to R + ε e^{At} f to force nonnegativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor maximum principle condition (Lemma 2.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose M_{αβ} evolves by ∂_t M = ΔM + u^i ∇_i M + N_{αβ} on M×[0,T], where N = P(M,h) is a polynomial in M using fiber metric h. If N_{αβ} v^α v^β ≥ 0 whenever M_{αβ} v^α v^β = 0, and M_{αβ} ≥ 0 at t=0, then M_{αβ} ≥ 0 for all 0 ≤ t ≤ T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses perturbation ˜M = M + ε e^{At} f h (with barrier f) and a contradiction argument; condition on N controls boundary behaviour at null directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of nonnegativity of curvature operator
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (Hamilton): Nonnegativity of the curvature operator M_{αβ} is preserved by the Ricci flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Lemma 2.1.3 to the evolution ∂_t M = ΔM + M^2 + M^# (where M^# is the quadratic algebraic term) to conclude nonnegativity is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of holomorphic bisectional curvature in Kähler-Ricci flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition: Under Kähler-Ricci flow, if the initial metric has positive (or nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature, the evolved metrics retain positive (or nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by Bando (n=3), Mok (compact general n), and Shi (noncompact); an analogue of Hamilton's tensor maximum principle adapted to Kähler curvature tensors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's strong maximum principle for tensors (Theorem 2.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a smooth symmetric bilinear form M_{αβ} evolving by ∂_t M = ΔM + N_{αβ} on a bounded connected Ω, if M_{αβ} ≥ 0 initially and N_{αβ} = P(M) satisfies N_{αβ} ≥ 0 when M_{αβ} ≥ 0, then there exists δ>0 so that on Ω×(0,δ) the rank of M_{αβ} is constant; the nullspace is invariant under parallel translation and in time and lies in the nullspace of N_{αβ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses heat evolution of an auxiliary positive function ρ, perturbation by ε e^{t}, and extension of null eigenvectors by parallel transport; gives structural rigidity of the zero-eigenspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of curvature operator is Lie subalgebra (Theorem 2.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the initial curvature operator is nonnegative, then for some short time the image of M_{αβ} is a Lie subalgebra of so(n) of constant rank, invariant under parallel translation and in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Theorem 2.2.1 together with algebraic identities for M^# and Ambrose–Singer holonomy considerations; gives restricted holonomy structure for equality cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced maximum principle for tensors (Theorem 2.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider PDE ∂_t σ = Δ_t σ + u^i (∇_t)_i σ + N(x,σ,t) on a bundle V over M with time-dependent connection. Let K⊂V be closed, invariant under parallel translation (H1), and with convex closed fibers K_x = V_x ∩ K (H2). If for every x and t the ODE dσ_x/dt = N(x,σ_x,t) preserves K_x, then any uniformly bounded PDE solution starting in K at t0 remains in K for later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem reduces PDE invariance questions to fiberwise ODE invariance; Lemmas 2.3.2–2.3.4 provide the technical bounds and ODE tangent-cone characterization needed in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-difference/ODE-to-PDE comparison lemma (Lemma 2.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ:[a,b]→R is Lipschitz and whenever φ(t) ≥ 0 one has dφ/dt ≤ C φ(t) (forward limsup derivative), and φ(a) ≤ 0, then φ(t) ≤ 0 on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Grönwall-type argument (use e^{-Ct}φ). Used to propagate sign constraints from differential inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative of a sup-function (Lemma 2.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ψ(x,t) be smooth on compact Y×[a,b]; set φ(t)=sup_{y∈Y} ψ(y,t). Then the forward derivative satisfies dφ/dt ≤ sup_{y with ψ(y,t)=φ(t)} ∂ψ/∂t (y,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to bound evolution of supremal quantities arising when reducing PDE behaviour to pointwise/ODE inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization when an ODE preserves a closed convex set (Lemma 2.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ODE dϕ/dt = N(ϕ,t) on R^n and closed convex Z⊂U an open set, the ODE preserves Z for all later times iff ϕ + N(ϕ,t) ∈ T_ϕ Z for all ϕ ∈ ∂Z and t, where T_ϕ Z is the tangent cone at ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, no support function l at boundary points has l(N(ϕ,t))>0; proof uses support function duality and distance function to Z. This is the fiberwise ODE condition used in the advanced maximum principle.
